questions.question: Explain three factors that affect the cost of a material and why gold is not used for household wiring.
questions.expected_answer: Rarity of the raw material; the energy and difficulty of extracting and processing it (aluminium needs a lot of electricity); transport distance; demand. Gold is an excellent conductor and does not corrode, but it is rare and extremely expensive, so copper and aluminium, which conduct well and cost far less, are used instead.

questions.question: Give two examples where colour has a function and two where texture has a function.
questions.expected_answer: Colour: white or light roofs reflect sunlight and keep buildings cooler; bright orange or yellow safety vests make people visible; coloured insulation identifies live, neutral and earth wires; red marks danger and fire equipment. Texture: smooth glazed tiles and stainless steel are easy to clean in kitchens and hospitals; rough or ridged surfaces give grip on steps, shoe soles and tyre treads; soft fabrics are comfortable for clothing and bedding.

questions.question: Compare thatch and corrugated iron for a rondavel roof under the headings cost, insulation, safety and durability, and justify a choice.
questions.expected_answer: Cost: thatch is cheap or free where grass grows locally; iron sheets are fairly cheap and quick to install. Insulation: thatch is a good insulator, cool in summer and warm in winter; thin iron conducts heat, so the room is hot in summer and cold in winter without a ceiling. Safety: thatch burns easily; iron is fireproof. Durability: thatch must be replaced every 15 to 25 years; galvanised iron lasts long but may rust. Any justified choice is acceptable, for example thatch for comfort and local availability with fire precautions, or iron for fire safety and rainwater collection with an insulating ceiling added.
